_note: RETRY of the three boss cues the gates refused. All three failed the SAME way and it is a
pattern worth recording: prompts whose subject is inherently low-frequency - fire, a missile
launch, a fleshy organic thing - come back as almost pure bass (0.027, 0.050, 0.055 of energy
above 2kHz against a 0.12 floor). ElevenLabs renders the body of the thing and not the crack.
The fix is to name the BRIGHT TRANSIENT first and the body second, and to raise retro_sr so
the band-limit is not also taking from a cue that had little to spare. Same correction that
rescued shield_hit_heavy, which went 0.000 -> 0.96 on exactly this change.

sounds.prompt: A sharp hissing ignition CRACK as pressurised fuel catches, bright and spitting, followed by a short roaring flame burst underneath. The crack is first and loudest. Crisp top end, dry, no reverb, no music. Retro arcade video game flame cannon shot.

A bright metallic CLANK of a launch rail releasing, then a sharp hissing rocket exhaust screaming away. Metallic and airy with plenty of high frequency detail, a thump only underneath. Dry, no reverb, no music. Retro arcade video game missile launch.

A sharp wet SNAP of tearing flesh, bright and sudden like a snapping tendon, with a brief hissing spray after it and a low growl beneath. The snap is immediate and is the loudest part. Dry, no reverb, no music. Retro arcade video game creature attack.
